name_reason: Fully compliant with fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. 'spell_handler' = role (dispatch-table entry). 'id_3' = spell_id literal 3 (valid spell ID, range 00h-23h) hardcoded as the spell_id arg passed to the worker; a meaningful domain ID that must be preserved, not an address residue. 'via_targeted_blink' accurately describes the worker fd2_execute_offensive_targeted_spell @ 0x21227, which is a TARGETED offensive spell (per-target damage loop over target_id_array) using the BLINK-OVERLAY animation variant (calls fd2_animate_spell_overlay_blink). No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Spell dispatch thunk for spell_id=3 (targeted offensive blink-overlay family): registered in the spell dispatch table @ 0x51D01 (entry index 3), delegates to fd2_execute_offensive_targeted_spell with spell_id literal 3.
logic_summary: Thin dispatch thunk. Pushes spell_id literal 3 plus the caller's num_targets and target_id_array, then (via a shared-tail JMP 0x2121A into sibling fd2_spell_handler_id_0_via_targeted_blink's tail) pushes caster_unit_id and CALLs fd2_execute_offensive_targeted_spell(caster_unit_id, 3, num_targets, target_id_array). The leading PUSH 0x14 + CALL __CHK is the Watcom stack-probe prologue (decompiles as __CHK(0x14, in_stack_00000000, ...) — a CRT stack-check artifact, not game logic). Net effect identical to the C source line: fd2_execute_offensive_targeted_spell(caster, 3, n_tgt, (int)tgt_arr).

params.name: caster_unit_id
params.semantics: Caster unit id; passed through unchanged to fd2_execute_offensive_targeted_spell as arg 1 (used to deduct MP and as animation source). Src declares it as 'caster'.
params.reason: Descriptive and accurate; no address residue. (Src uses the shorter 'caster' but both are clean; rename, if ever desired for src/Ghidra unification, is a Stage-2 concern, not flagged here.)

params.name: num_targets
params.semantics: Number of targets; passed through as arg 3 to the worker (loop bound for the per-target damage loop). Src declares it as 'n_tgt'.
params.reason: Descriptive and accurate; no address residue.

params.name: target_id_array
params.semantics: Pointer to the array of target unit ids; passed through as arg 4 to the worker (indexed in the per-target damage loop). Src declares it as 'tgt_arr' (uint8 *).
params.reason: Descriptive and accurate; no address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value (cdecl void). Effect is entirely via the delegated worker call.

notes: src comment: this handler is documented collectively via the family header '/* === Targeted blink family (id 0-3, 8) === */' (spell.c line 24) plus the file-top pattern table (lines 1-17). That is concise, correct, and at the right altitude for these 5 near-identical thunks; no dedicated per-function block exists or is needed, so spell.c was NOT modified (comment_verdict=keep). Ghidra plate is detailed, accurate, and consistent with the src understanding (dispatch table xref 0x51D0D = 0x51D01+0xC = entry 3 verified by reading the table; shared-tail JMP 0x2121A and worker semantics confirmed by decompiling 0x21206 and 0x21227), so plate left untouched (ghidra_plate_action=none). The decompiled in_stack_00000000 fed to __CHK is the standard Watcom stack-probe signature shared by all sibling thunks, not a bug. Only the shard file is staged for this commit; spell.c unchanged.
